svg.title: Why macOS writes through two paths
svg.desc: macOS has no registry, so the Mac build writes through two paths at the same time. The upper one: a terminal reads the shell hook on startup (written into ~/.zshenv and ~/.zshrc), the hook loads ~/.envproxy/proxy.env, and the variables take effect. The lower one: an app launched from the Dock is covered by launchctl setenv, which hands the variables to the whole session. Both paths write the same 9 variables and move together; 5 of them are the standard spellings and 4 are lowercase, because macOS is case sensitive and the two spellings are separate variables.
